chapters.title: Release artifact integrity
chapters.summary: A self-update path is a release transaction: identify one immutable version, select one exact platform artifact, verify its digest, and report whether installation actually completed.

sections.title: Select exact release inputs
sections.summary: Match a normalized semantic version and exact target-specific filename; reject missing, duplicate, option-shaped, oversized, or ambiguous inputs before replacing anything.

sections.title: Verify and report the outcome
sections.summary: Bound downloads and diagnostics, verify SHA-256 before staging, use atomic replacement where the operating system permits it, and distinguish a staged file from an installed update.

key_facts.statement: Deployment is a repeatable transition with observable preconditions and outcomes.
Define artifact identity, compatibility, health gates, rollout, and rollback.
A process that starts successfully is not necessarily serving healthy behavior.
An updater should select one exact versioned platform asset and its exact checksum companion rather than accept substring or first-match selection.
Checksum verification must occur before installation, and a staged executable must not be reported as an installed update.
Build jobs should use read-only repository permissions; only the release publication job needs contents write authority.
